hf: Top model repository’s downloads over the previous 30 days, checked Nov 18. For small-model leaderboard publishers, the linked submission is used.
gh: Lifetime stars on the relevant linked project or the most-starred public, non-fork repo of the listed organization. Includes tools as well as models.
requests: Mean daily share of Vercel AI Gateway requests, Nov 11–17. The average gives each day equal weight.
spend: Mean daily share of spending on Vercel AI Gateway, Nov 11–17. The average gives each day equal weight.
tokens: Mean daily share of Vercel AI Gateway tokens, Nov 11–17. The average gives each day equal weight.
imageCount: Mean daily share of Vercel AI Gateway images generated, Nov 11–17. The average gives each day equal weight.
videoCount: Mean daily share of Vercel AI Gateway videos generated, Nov 11–17. The average gives each day equal weight.

labs.name: 0arch.io
labs.focus: Trained Kisoku, a one-person experiment in building a language model that can read long inputs.

team.background: Pretrained and tested Kisoku 1.6B as an individual research project.

innovation.assessment: Kisoku started as a small model trained from scratch. Its creator extended it to read up to 64,000 tokens at once and published the weights and training details. That gives other developers a concrete example of how far one person can push a model with limited computing resources.

labs.name: Aaru
labs.focus: Builds simulated populations to explore how people might respond to a product, message, or policy.

people.names: Cameron Fink, Ned Koh, John Kessler

innovation.example: Simulated answers compared with published surveys
innovation.assessment: Aaru generates synthetic survey answers and compares their shares with published survey results. Across 2,993 questions, Aaru reports a mean error of 2.78 percentage points after adjusting for sampling noise, and 3.53 points before the adjustment.

labs.name: AGI Inc
labs.focus: Trains models to operate apps directly on a device.

people.names: Div Garg, Steve Frey, Naman Garg

innovation.evidence: Company model page and benchmark result
innovation.assessment: AGI-0 is a small model that reads a phone screen and chooses actions such as tapping or typing. AGI Inc. reports that its newest model configuration completed all 116 tasks in the AndroidWorld benchmark.

labs.name: Answer.AI
labs.focus: Co-developed ModernBERT, a model for understanding and searching text.

innovation.example: ModernBERT, joint work with LightOn and collaborators
innovation.assessment: ModernBERT reads up to 8,192 tokens and builds a representation of the text for tools such as search and classification. Answer.AI, LightOn, and collaborators report competitive or better results than older encoders on classification and retrieval tests, with faster processing in their setup.

labs.name: Applied Compute
labs.focus: Helps companies train open models on examples from their own workflows.

people.names: Yash Patil, Rhythm Garg, Linden Li

innovation.example: Claygent routes requests to cheaper models when it can
innovation.assessment: Applied Compute trained a small model to choose which larger or smaller model should answer a request. In Clay’s deployment, the companies reported up to 47% lower inference costs while maintaining answer quality on their tests.

labs.name: Arcee AI
labs.focus: Trains open language models that use only part of the network for each piece of text.

people.names: Mark McQuade, Jacob Solawetz, Brian Benedict

innovation.example: Trinity-Large-Thinking adds reasoning to a sparse model
innovation.assessment: Only part of Trinity’s network runs for each piece of text. Arcee trained the Thinking version to reason before answering and released its weights. Its report compares it with the earlier preview on coding, reasoning, and tool use.

labs.name: Arda
labs.focus: Builds software for industrial engineering and manufacturing workflows.

people.names: Bob McGrew, Augustus Odena, Alex Mark, Jakob Frick

innovation.assessment: Arda shows software for organizing design, planning, and production work. Its site explains how the software fits into factory workflows. It gives too little detail to evaluate a model or training method.

labs.name: Axiom Math
labs.focus: Trains AI to write mathematical proofs a computer can check step by step.

innovation.example: Lean-checked proof of the Lyons–White conjecture
innovation.assessment: Moving a random walk faster might seem to bring it closer to equilibrium. Axiom’s mathematicians proved that it depends on how distance from equilibrium is measured. The release includes a Lean formalization readers can check.

labs.name: Basecamp Research
labs.focus: Develops foundation models for therapeutic research.

innovation.assessment: Basecamp announced EDEN as a model for therapeutic research. The release sets out the research direction. How useful the model is in the clinic depends on follow-up studies.

labs.name: Bedrock Robotics
labs.focus: Retrofits excavators with sensors and software so they can move earth under operator supervision.

people.names: Boris Sofman, Kevin Peterson, Tom Eliaz, Ajay Gummalla

innovation.assessment: Bedrock says its excavators moved more than 70,000 cubic yards of earth on a manufacturing site with Sundt under supervised autonomy. The report gives the volume moved. It leaves open how often an operator had to intervene.

labs.fit_note: Public deployments show working excavation autonomy. Its public sources give less detail on any original control or training method.

labs.name: Bioptimus
labs.focus: Develops the H-Optimus family of models for examining images of tissue samples.

innovation.example: H-Optimus-1 recognizes patterns in pathology slides
innovation.assessment: H-Optimus-1 turns microscope images of tissue into representations that other models can use. Bioptimus released the weights and compared the model with H-Optimus-0 and others on 13 pathology tasks, from individual image tiles to whole slides.

labs.name: Cartesia
labs.focus: Builds speech models designed to start talking quickly and explores new ways for models to process audio.

people.names: Karan Goel, Albert Gu, Arjun Desai, Brandon Yang

innovation.assessment: Sonic-3.6 turns text into speech while the audio is streaming. Cartesia reports a reply time under 90 milliseconds and generation at 132 characters per second, compared with 68 for Sonic-3 Conversational.

labs.name: Causal Labs
labs.focus: Starts with weather forecasting to study models that could work across different physical systems.

innovation.example: Physics models starting with weather forecasting
innovation.assessment: The research question is whether one modeling approach can learn how different physical systems evolve. Weather is the first example. The announcement explains what Causal Labs plans to build. Forecast comparisons with existing weather models would show how well the idea works.

labs.fit_note: The lab has described a research program for physics models. The linked launch outlines the approach and names the first model as future work.

labs.name: Chai Discovery
labs.focus: Builds models that predict the shapes of molecules and how they fit together.

people.names: Joshua Meier, Jack Dent, Matthew McPartlon, Jacques Boitreaud

innovation.assessment: Chai-1 gives researchers a predicted shape for several kinds of molecules using one model. That lets them study possible interactions before running experiments. Its published comparisons measure the quality of those structure predictions.

labs.name: Core Automation
labs.focus: Experiments with new AI architectures and ways to train models, including using GPUs in different data centers for a single training run.

team.background: Team members previously led reinforcement-learning research at OpenAI and pretraining for Gemini.

people.names: Jerry Tworek, Rohan Anil, Joanne Jang, Anmol Gulati, Julia Villagra

innovation.assessment: Core trained a 32B model across two clusters about 9,000 miles apart. The computers trained locally between exchanges. At the same compute budget, the two-cluster run had about 1% lower prediction loss on two coding tests than standard training on one cluster, according to Core.

artifacts.label: The Hitchhiker’s Guide to Training on Compute Islands
What the Models Learned in One Layer Deeper

labs.name: Corma
labs.focus: Trains models for defensive cybersecurity workflows.

innovation.assessment: Corma describes models it wants to train and use for cyber defense. The public material gives the intended use. A comparison with existing defensive tools is still missing.

labs.name: CuspAI
labs.focus: Builds AI tools and research partnerships for materials discovery.

innovation.assessment: The AI Materials Foundry brings materials researchers and industrial partners into one discovery program. The announcement explains how they work together. Comparisons showing what the underlying models add are still missing.

labs.name: Decart
labs.focus: Builds models that generate the next frame of a game in response to player input.

people.names: Dean Leitersdorf, Moshe Shalev, Orian Leitersdorf

innovation.assessment: Oasis, built by Decart and Etched, generates each next frame of a Minecraft-style world from keyboard and mouse input. The team released 500M model weights and hosted a live demo of a larger version. GameNGen is linked as earlier work on interactive game simulation.

labs.fit_note: Oasis shows original work on interactive video generation with Etched. Decart also develops and sells creative tools built around its models.

labs.name: Deep Cogito
labs.focus: Trains reasoning models to learn from the paths they try while solving problems.

innovation.example: Cogito v2.1 uses shorter reasoning traces
innovation.assessment: Deep Cogito started with a DeepSeek base model and trained it further on reasoning. In the lab’s test suite, v2.1 used fewer output tokens on average than models with similar scores. The lab released the weights.

labs.name: Dream Labs
labs.focus: Trains models to perform tasks on robots they have never encountered during training.

innovation.assessment: Dream-1 predicts a short sequence of visuals and robot movements from its camera view. The release shows it trying tasks on robot types left out of training, including folding a box on a KAIST robot. These are transfer examples with varying success across demos.

labs.name: Dyna Robotics
labs.focus: Tests whether robots can learn to handle objects by watching people do the same work.

innovation.example: Dyna-2 tests how human video helps robot learning
innovation.assessment: Dyna trained models on between 1,000 and one million hours of human video, then tested their predictions on recordings from robots they had never seen. More video helped on those tests. The lab also tested real robot performance after giving each version the same robot training data.

labs.name: Eka Robotics
labs.focus: Builds robots that use both cameras and force sensors to handle objects.

innovation.example: Eka combines camera views and force readings
innovation.assessment: Eka trains robots to sense how hard they are pushing as well as what they see. The team reports about 1,500 picks an hour across objects outside its training set, compared with about 600 for its human baseline in the same picking comparison.

labs.name: EleutherAI
labs.focus: Studies how language models change during training.

innovation.assessment: Pythia gives researchers saved copies of models at many points during training. Because the models follow the same training setup at different sizes, researchers can compare when a skill appears and whether larger models learn it sooner.

labs.name: EquiLibre Technologies
labs.focus: Applies techniques from game-playing AI to training models for live trading.

team.people: Martin Schmid, Matej Moravcik, Rudolf Kadlec
team.background: The founders came from AI and game-playing research. Their published work includes DeepStack and Player of Games.

people.names: Martin Schmid, Matej Moravcik, Rudolf Kadlec

innovation.assessment: EquiLibre says it builds reinforcement-learning models for live trading. The team draws on earlier work in game-playing AI. Its public overview describes the direction, and details about the training method and returns are private.

labs.name: Essential AI
labs.focus: Trains and releases language models so other researchers can study how they were built.

innovation.example: Rnj-1 releases the base and instruction-tuned models
innovation.assessment: Essential AI trained an 8-billion-parameter language model using a design based on Gemma 3 and extended its context to 32,000 tokens. It published both the base and instruction-tuned versions, so researchers can inspect the starting model and what it became after further training.

labs.name: FieldAI
labs.focus: Builds robot models that plan routes and work in unfamiliar industrial sites while accounting for uncertainty.

innovation.evidence: Company architecture overview and deployment announcement
innovation.assessment: FieldAI’s model tracks how sure it is about the terrain and obstacles. If a robot can’t judge an obstacle, it can slow down, take a different route, or collect more sensor readings. Kajima announced a full-scale deployment of FieldAI’s system on construction sites. FieldAI describes the model at a high level.

labs.name: Fish Audio
labs.focus: Develops multilingual speech generation models and releases model weights.

innovation.example: Fish Audio S2 expressive multilingual speech
innovation.assessment: Fish Audio’s S2 release lets users control how speech sounds in several languages. Earlier systems offered expressive speech too. S2 makes those controls available in a model that other researchers can download.

labs.name: Flapping Airplanes
labs.focus: Looks for ways to teach a model more from the same amount of training data.

team.people: Ben Spector, Asher Spector, Aidan Smith
team.background: The team works across GPU kernels, pretraining, post-training, and inference.

people.names: Ben Spector, Asher Spector, Aidan Smith

innovation.example: Data-efficient training program and GPU megakernel work
innovation.assessment: Flapping Airplanes wants models to learn more from each example. Its lead investor describes a pretraining run and code that combines GPU operations to reduce idle time. The account does not give a model result or a comparison showing how much less training data the lab’s approach needs.

labs.fit_note: The investor describes a pretraining run and GPU work. The linked account gives no lab-authored technical release or model result to evaluate.

labs.name: Flourish
labs.focus: Reportedly researches brain-inspired approaches to more energy-efficient AI.

innovation.assessment: Flourish has described a research direction inspired by how the brain computes. The public material leaves the model design, energy use, and test results open.

labs.name: Fractale
labs.focus: Trained a small language model to test whether it could learn what to remember.

innovation.assessment: Fractale-350M is a small language model released as part of an experiment in learned memory. The question is whether the model can learn what to store for later use. The release lets others inspect it. Testing with and without the memory would isolate its effect.

labs.name: Fundamental
labs.focus: Trained NEXUS to make predictions from tables across different kinds of problems.

mentions.title: Fundamental nomination
mentions.author: TheRealDanSaedi
mentions.note: A reply arguing for Fundamental. The live list already carries the company.

innovation.assessment: NEXUS learns from data organized into rows and columns before it is given a particular prediction task. The goal is to reuse what it learned on a new table. A useful comparison would test whether it carries that knowledge to unfamiliar tables better than existing tools.

labs.name: Generalist AI
labs.focus: Trains robot models on recordings that combine multiple kinds of sensor data.

people.names: Pete Florence, Andy Zeng, Andrew Barry

innovation.example: GEN-1.5 learns a physical task from one demonstration
innovation.assessment: A short recording shows the robot what to do, such as opening a jar, without retraining the model. Generalist reports 59% average success across ten short tasks from one example and 83% after fine-tuning on about five minutes of examples per task.

labs.name: Genesis AI
labs.focus: Trains robots to handle objects precisely using examples from people and robots.

innovation.assessment: Genesis wants a model that can learn how to handle objects from different sources of examples. Human demonstrations and robot data together give the model more ways to see how a task is done. The released demos show what it can do on selected manipulation tasks.

labs.name: Genmo
labs.focus: Trained Mochi, an open model that generates video from text.

innovation.assessment: Mochi gives the video and text parts of its diffusion model different amounts of computation. Genmo’s open preview generates up to 5.4 seconds of 480p video at 30 frames per second. The release includes comparisons on motion and how closely clips follow prompts.

labs.name: GigaAI
labs.focus: Trains robots to use predictions of how a scene will change to choose better movements.

innovation.assessment: GigaBrain-0.7 separates three jobs: interpreting the instruction and scene, predicting how the scene could change, and turning that prediction into robot movements. An earlier experiment used predicted outcomes during training and reported gains on physical tasks including folding laundry and packing boxes. The newer release tests how well the design carries over to different robot hardware.

labs.name: Goodfire
labs.focus: Tests teaching models which clues to rely on while they are being trained.

people.names: Eric Ho, Daniel Balsam, Tom McGrath

innovation.assessment: Goodfire looks for patterns inside a model that correspond to specific clues, then changes how much the model learns to rely on them. In one study, an X-ray model had learned to spot a chest drain as a shortcut for a collapsed lung. Goodfire reports reducing the model’s reliance on that shortcut during training.

labs.name: Gradium
labs.focus: Builds text-to-speech models that run on a phone, laptop, or other local hardware.

people.names: Neil Zeghidour, Olivier Teboul, Laurent Mazaré, Alexandre Défossez

innovation.assessment: Phonon runs text-to-speech on a device’s own processor. Gradium reports that its 31M model started speaking in 38 milliseconds and ran 3.7 times faster than real time on a Raspberry Pi 5. The lab released weights and inference code.

labs.name: Gravis Robotics
labs.focus: Develops learned controllers and retrofit autonomy for excavators and other heavy machinery.

people.names: Ryan Luke Johns, Dominic Jud, Marco Hutter

innovation.evidence: Peer-reviewed joint research and machine demos
innovation.example: Simulation-trained control of a five-tonne loader
innovation.assessment: Gravis and collaborators trained controllers in a simulator calibrated with measurements from a real John Deere loader. On the actual machine, a learned controller could balance the loader on two wheels and drive it over uneven ground. The experiment shows learned control of a specific machine and set of maneuvers.

labs.fit_note: The team contributed to original learned-control research on heavy equipment. Its public work centers on adapting autonomy to construction machines.

labs.name: Guide Labs
labs.focus: Builds language models that let developers see and adjust the influence of named concepts on the text they generate.

innovation.assessment: Steerling-8B was trained to use named concepts as part of choosing what words to write. Developers can see how much a concept contributed to a passage and strengthen or weaken its influence as the model writes. In one demo, increasing the coffee concept made a generic checklist prompt produce text about roasting and brewing coffee.

labs.name: H Company
labs.focus: Trains Holo models to identify and interact with items on a computer or phone screen.

people.names: Charles Kantor, Laurent Sifre, Karl Tuyls, Daan Wierstra, Julien Perolat

innovation.example: Holo2 desktop and mobile computer-use models
innovation.assessment: Holo2 looks at a screen and identifies the element an agent should click. H reports 66.1% accuracy on ScreenSpot-Pro, a benchmark for locating controls in professional software.

labs.name: Hark
labs.focus: Builds Handoff, a personal AI that can work in the apps on a user’s computer.

innovation.assessment: Handoff uses websites by looking at the page and choosing actions such as clicking and scrolling. Hark reports that it averaged eight percentage points above GPT-5.4 across three browser-use evaluations, including its own tests.

labs.name: Harmonic
labs.focus: Trains Aristotle to search for mathematical proofs and check them with Lean.

innovation.example: Aristotle tackled the 2025 International Mathematical Olympiad
innovation.assessment: Aristotle combines a proof search system with a geometry solver and uses Lean to check formal proofs. Harmonic’s paper reports a score equivalent to a gold medal on the 2025 Olympiad problems.

labs.name: HiDream.ai
labs.focus: Develops open image generation models, including the HiDream-I1 architecture.

innovation.assessment: HiDream-I1 is an open image generator that uses only some of its specialist network blocks at each step. The team published the weights and the report’s image evaluations, which measure the complete generator.

labs.name: Imbue
labs.focus: Now develops coding-agent tools and previously reported training a 70B language model from scratch.

innovation.assessment: Imbue completed a model training run and released tools for training and testing models. Other researchers can inspect what the team built and use the tools in their own experiments.

labs.name: Inception Labs
labs.focus: Builds Mercury, a language model that can revise several parts of an answer in parallel.

mentions.title: Inception Labs nomination
mentions.author: sarahcat21
mentions.note: A reply to the early crowdsourced list naming Inception Labs.

people.names: Stefano Ermon, Aditya Grover, Volodymyr Kuleshov

innovation.example: Mercury 3 scales diffusion for text generation
innovation.assessment: Mercury uses diffusion to refine groups of tokens together as it writes. Inception reports that Mercury 3 reached about 1,070 tokens per second on NVIDIA GPUs while improving on earlier Mercury models in its tests.

labs.name: Ineffable Intelligence
labs.focus: Researches models that improve by trying actions and learning from the results.

team.background: Silver is a UCL professor and formerly led reinforcement learning at Google DeepMind.

innovation.assessment: David Silver’s research plan is to train agents through experience. The agent tries an action, gets feedback on the result, and uses that to learn which actions to repeat. The public statement describes the approach ahead of a model result.

labs.fit_note: The public research statement explains how the team wants to train agents from experience. It describes the program at an early stage.

labs.name: Intelligent Machines
labs.focus: Reportedly develops robots for complex industrial work.

innovation.assessment: Public reporting describes the team’s industrial robot prototypes. Details about the underlying models and how they perform are still limited.

labs.name: Isara Labs
labs.focus: Builds simulations in which many AI agents make decisions and respond to one another.

innovation.assessment: The model uses a group of agents to explore how individual choices might add up to an outcome. That gives users a way to explore scenarios. Evidence from real outcomes would show when those simulations are useful as forecasts.

labs.name: Isomorphic Labs
labs.focus: Co-developed AlphaFold 3 to predict how molecules are shaped and how they interact.

innovation.example: AlphaFold 3, joint work with Google DeepMind
innovation.assessment: AlphaFold 3 predicts the shapes of more kinds of molecules and how they fit together. The paper compares its predictions with earlier tools. Isomorphic Labs and Google DeepMind developed it jointly.

labs.name: Kohaku Lab
labs.focus: Releases image models and experiments with cheaper ways to train them.
labs.size: The lab lists eight people, including two core team members.

team.background: An open research group publishing diffusion models and tools.

innovation.example: Open diffusion experiments and training tools
innovation.assessment: Kohaku shares models and tools for training image generators. Other researchers can use the releases to see what made an experiment practical and try the methods on their own compute. Comparisons with similar open image models are still limited.

labs.name: Kronos
labs.focus: Trained a model to forecast prices from sequences of market data.

innovation.example: Tokenizer and model tailored to financial price and volume data
innovation.assessment: Kronos turns numbers such as price and trading volume into a sequence it can learn to continue. Its paper reports that predicted prices tracked the actual ordering better than the best general-purpose time-series model it tested. This measures forecasting performance on the authors’ data.

labs.name: Kyutai
labs.focus: Built Moshi, a voice model that can listen and speak at the same time.

innovation.example: Moshi full-duplex speech with the Mimi codec
innovation.assessment: Moshi processes the user’s voice and the model’s speech as two streams that run at the same time. That lets it handle an interruption while it is still talking. Kyutai also reports an audio delay of about a fifth of a second in its test setup.

labs.name: Levanto Labs
labs.focus: Builds Sage, a model for choosing an answer from a defined set of options about text or images.

innovation.assessment: Sage is designed for decisions an application can act on directly. The application specifies the possible answers, and the model makes a choice based on text or an image. Levanto has published results on the tasks the model was designed for.

labs.name: Lila Sciences
labs.focus: Develops AI systems that work with automated scientific laboratories.

people.names: Geoffrey von Maltzahn, Molly Gibson, Noubar Afeyan, Rafael Gómez-Bombarelli

innovation.example: An AI-guided lab screened catalysts for green hydrogen
innovation.assessment: Lila’s system used the results of past experiments to choose which materials to test next. The company reports screening 2,942 candidates and finding a cheaper palladium-based material that matched a ruthenium benchmark in its acid stability tests.

labs.name: Liquid AI
labs.focus: Designs models that can run quickly on hardware such as phones and laptops.

people.names: Ramin Hasani, Mathias Lechner, Alexander Amini, Daniela Rus

innovation.assessment: LFM2 uses cheaper calculations for nearby words and reserves a few layers for comparing words across the full input. The design is meant to keep models fast on phones and laptops. In one Galaxy S25 test, Liquid reports that its 350M model generated text about twice as fast as Granite-4.0-350M.

labs.name: Luma AI
labs.focus: Trains video and image models and deploys them through creative products.

people.names: Amit Jain, Alex Yu, Alberto Taiuti

innovation.assessment: Luma released Ray3 and built a video-making workflow around it. The release shows the tools working together. It leaves open how much of the improvement comes from Ray3’s reasoning component.

labs.name: Lvmin Zhang
labs.focus: Builds FramePack to keep the memory used by a video generator in check as a clip gets longer.

team.background: Researcher-led, with academic collaborators.

innovation.assessment: FramePack compresses earlier frames according to how much the next frame needs them. That lets a video model work with a longer history in the same amount of memory. The joint paper also tests ways to reduce visual errors that accumulate over a long clip.

labs.name: Machenta
labs.focus: Trains robots in simulation to pick up new physical tasks from a single demonstration.

innovation.example: Instant robot learning from one example
innovation.assessment: Machenta trains its model entirely in simulation. In the company’s demos, an operator shows a real robot a new task once. The robot then attempts it using that demonstration as an instruction, without a fresh round of training. This is early evidence on the tasks shown.

labs.name: Magic
labs.focus: Studies how to let a coding model work with very long inputs, including up to 100 million tokens.

innovation.assessment: Magic reports that LTM-2-mini processed very long inputs in HashHop, a test that asks a model to follow a chain of random key–value pairs. The researchers released the test code. The experiment measures long-range retrieval in synthetic inputs.

labs.name: Mantic
labs.focus: Trains models that assign probabilities to future events.

team.background: The team includes researchers and engineers with backgrounds at Google DeepMind and Palantir.

innovation.assessment: Mantic gives a base model additional practice on questions with outcomes that can be checked. It wants the model to get better at judging the odds of events. In a technical guest post, Mantic’s researchers report that the adapted model made better forecasts than the base model on their test questions.

labs.name: Maritaca AI
labs.focus: Develops Portuguese language models in the Sabiá family and documents language-specific training.

innovation.assessment: Maritaca continued training Sabiá-4 and Sabiazinho-4 on Portuguese and Brazilian legal material. Its report compares them with earlier Sabiá models and reports gains on legal document drafting, multi-turn conversation, and tasks requiring tools.

labs.name: Mimic Robotics
labs.focus: Uses video prediction to teach robots precise assembly with fewer recorded robot demonstrations.

people.names: Stefan Weirich, Stephan-Daniel Gravert, Elvis Nava, Robert Katzschmann

innovation.assessment: Mimic and BMW trained FLUX-mimic to predict what the robot will see and how it should move. Starting with a model pretrained on video reduces the need for examples recorded on the robot. They tested it on assembly tasks such as mounting a control unit onto a bracket.

labs.name: Mind Robotics
labs.focus: Trains industrial robots using examples collected on manufacturing lines.

innovation.assessment: Mind Robotics plans to use examples from production lines to train robots for manufacturing work, including through its relationship with Rivian. Its public material describes the approach and deployment plans. A comparable task evaluation remains open.

labs.name: Mnemonic Labs
labs.focus: Trains a model for quantitative trading directly on market activity.

team.background: Both founders studied at MIT. Videh did quant research at Citadel and Walleye. Kalki worked at Tower Research Capital.

innovation.assessment: Mnemonic’s bet is that the sequence of events in a market is itself something a model can learn from. The founders say they built a model architecture and started training it on that kind of data. The public launch describes the approach. How well it forecasts or trades is still open.

labs.fit_note: The founders describe a market-native architecture and an ongoing training run. The launch gives an account of the approach before sharing model results.

labs.name: ModelBest
labs.focus: Builds compact models that can handle different kinds of input, including text and images.

innovation.evidence: Model card, release notes and open weights
innovation.example: MiniCPM5-1B publishes a compact language model and training data
innovation.assessment: OpenBMB’s one-billion-parameter model is sized for local use. Its release compares the model with similarly sized models from Liquid and Qwen on coding and tool use. It publishes weights and major parts of the training data.

labs.name: nanochat
labs.focus: Provides a small, documented example of how to train a chat model from scratch.

team.background: Individual-led project with community contributors.

innovation.assessment: nanochat shows the steps from raw training text to a model you can chat with. Its speedrun tracks how quickly each version reaches a defined quality target, with the exact code revision attached. Other developers can repeat a run and see whether their changes help.

labs.name: Nof1
labs.focus: Develops AI for financial markets and uses trading competitions to compare how models make decisions.

team.background: Its team includes alumni of DeepMind, Two Sigma, Citadel, and Bridgewater.

innovation.example: Alpha Arena compares models in one live trading run
innovation.assessment: Nof1 gave models from several providers the same starting capital and rules, then published their trades and results. A single market run is a test of those entrants in those conditions. It leaves open how a separately trained Nof1 model would perform.

labs.name: Nomic AI
labs.focus: Extended its 2024 text-search research to engineering drawings and specs. Its AI tools now review and draft project documents.
labs.status: Focuses on AI for architecture, engineering, and construction

innovation.assessment: AEC-Bench has 196 tasks for testing how AI agents read engineering drawings and combine information across construction documents. Nomic reports that adding its document tools improved drawing navigation scores by about 19 points on average. It released the tasks and evaluation code.
innovation.note: Embed Text v1 (February 2024) learned to match passages by meaning. Embed Multimodal (April 2025) extended that search to PDFs, charts, and images. That helps Nomic’s agents find the drawing or specification they need to review a project file.

labs.name: Nous Research
labs.focus: Builds open models and explores how to train them across computers with slow connections.

people.names: Jeffrey Quesnelle, Karan Malhotra, Teknium, Shivani Mitra

innovation.evidence: Company training comparison, code and weights
innovation.example: Hermes 4.3 is trained across 24 separate nodes
innovation.assessment: Nous used Psyche to train a language model across separate computers. It overlapped network transfers with computation so the machines spent less time waiting. The lab reports similar training throughput to its centralized run and released both model versions.

labs.name: Occiglot
labs.focus: Tests how further training changes a language model’s ability to work across European languages.

innovation.assessment: Occiglot continued training a Mistral 7B model on English, German, French, Spanish, and Italian. It published the resulting weights and documents how it evaluates the multilingual model.

labs.name: Odyssey
labs.focus: Develops interactive world models that generate video in response to actions.

innovation.example: Odyssey-3 predicts interactive video with physical consistency
innovation.assessment: Odyssey-3 generates the next scene as a user or agent acts. On the Physics-IQ Verified video test, the Pro model scored 66.1 according to the cited leaderboard. That score measures physical consistency on the test clips.

labs.name: Overworld
labs.focus: Builds models that generate game environments as players interact with them.

innovation.example: Waypoint-1.5 streams an interactive generated environment
innovation.assessment: Waypoint-1.5 makes the next part of a scene in response to a player’s input. Overworld says it reduced repeated calculations across frames so the model can respond in real time on supported consumer GPUs.

labs.name: Pathway
labs.focus: Tests a language model that keeps a running memory as it reads.

people.names: Zuzanna Stamirowska, Jan Chorowski, Adrian Kosowski

innovation.assessment: Dragon Hatchling carries earlier information in connections that update as it reads. The authors report results comparable to GPT-2-style Transformers on language and translation tasks when trained on the same data at sizes from 10 million to one billion parameters.

labs.name: Perceptron
labs.focus: Trains one model to interpret video, track task progress, and control robots.

innovation.example: Isaac 0.5 learns from video and robot demonstrations
innovation.assessment: Isaac 0.5 can answer questions about a video, tell how far along a task is, and generate robot movements. Perceptron compared different mixes of ordinary video and robot demonstrations. Perceptron reports that with more ordinary video, it needed fewer hours of people operating robots to reach the same error level when predicting recorded movements on held-out data.

labs.name: Periodic Labs
labs.focus: Trains models on physical-science experiment data. Its Neon model analyzes lab results.

team.background: The founding team includes contributors to ChatGPT, OpenAI Operator, and DeepMind’s GNoME and MatterGen.

innovation.example: Periodic Neon interprets experimental diffraction patterns
innovation.assessment: Neon reads the patterns produced when X-rays scatter from a sample and uses them to infer its structure. Periodic trained it on its own laboratory measurements and reports results on 198 experimental measurements from chemical systems held out of training.

labs.name: Physical Intelligence
labs.focus: Trains one robot model to understand instructions and control different kinds of robots.

people.names: Sergey Levine, Karol Hausman, Lachy Groom

innovation.example: π0.7 learns to follow step-by-step robot instructions
innovation.assessment: Physical Intelligence trained the model with descriptions of both the task and how to perform it. The lab showed a robot using an air fryer with step-by-step coaching. A separate policy trained from those instructions then generated the steps for an autonomous run.

labs.name: Physical Superintelligence
labs.focus: Builds research systems that search for and verify results in physics and mathematics.

people.names: Matt Pines, Alex Wissner-Gross, Alex Klokus; Alessandro Morari

innovation.assessment: David Turturean used PSI’s research system and a non-public Anthropic model to find a proof of a quantum computing conjecture open since 2008. PSI released a version checked by the Lean proof assistant. Four researchers published a separate exposition after studying the proof.
innovation.note: PSI describes plans to use physics checks and experiments as feedback to train its own virtual physicists. Mostly reflects the public evidence so far. PSI has demonstrated its research system, while evidence of a new model architecture or training result from PSI itself is still limited.

artifacts.label: PSI’s physics research and training plans

labs.name: Pleias
labs.focus: Builds small reasoning models and publishes how it sources the training material.

innovation.evidence: Weights, training dataset and lab evaluations
innovation.assessment: Pleias trained Baguettotron on SYNTH, a public dataset of generated training examples. The release shares both the model and dataset. Its model card tests reasoning and retrieval against other small models.

labs.name: Pluralis Research
labs.focus: Researches decentralized training under low-bandwidth constraints and releases experimental models.

innovation.example: Factored Gossip DiLoCo reduces waiting in distributed training
innovation.assessment: When computers train together across slow connections, they can spend time waiting for one another. Pluralis splits synchronization into a step that can run during training and a step that brings the computers back into agreement. In tests on models up to about a billion parameters, the team reports better hardware utilization than standard DiLoCo with similar training progress.

labs.name: Poetiq
labs.focus: Builds a system that uses existing language models to propose and test answers to puzzles.

team.background: The founders previously worked at Google and DeepMind.

innovation.evidence: Independent benchmark verification and solver code
innovation.assessment: Poetiq’s solver asks an existing model to write a program for a grid puzzle, checks it against the examples, and feeds failures back for revision. ARC Prize verified 54% on the semi-private ARC-AGI-2 set at about $31 per problem.

labs.name: Poolside
labs.focus: Trains coding models by giving them practice in software-engineering environments.

innovation.example: Laguna XS 2.1 improves multilingual code repair
innovation.assessment: Laguna XS 2.1 keeps the previous model’s design, which uses about 3 billion of its 33 billion parameters for each token. Poolside reports that additional training raised its score on the multilingual SWE-bench code-repair test from 57.7% to 63.1%.

labs.name: Prime Intellect
labs.focus: Splits the work of generating practice answers across computers in different locations.

innovation.evidence: Technical release, training code and weights
innovation.example: INTELLECT-3 publishes its reasoning post-training setup
innovation.assessment: Prime Intellect used an asynchronous training system to post-train a 106-billion-parameter model based on GLM-4.5-Air. Workers generate attempts at tasks while the trainer updates the model, so neither has to wait for every other worker. The release includes the weights, training code, and evaluation environments.

labs.fit_note: INTELLECT-2 documents original distributed training research. Prime Intellect also runs a broader compute and training platform.

labs.name: Project Prometheus
labs.focus: Reportedly builds AI for engineering, manufacturing, and physical systems.

innovation.assessment: Public reports describe engineering and manufacturing as the project’s focus. A published model or technical result from the lab is still missing.

labs.name: QFI Labs
labs.focus: Trains financial language models on disclosures, news, and research.

innovation.assessment: QFI describes training on financial documents. The public material has yet to show how well its model does on financial tasks compared with a general text model.

labs.fit_note: The lab describes financial model training and its research workflow. Its public examples are illustrative and leave the model’s contribution open.

labs.name: QSI Labs
labs.focus: Researches models of financial markets and trains AI agents to make decisions in market-specific environments.

innovation.example: Research program for market models and RL agents
innovation.assessment: QSI describes two related ideas. A market model would learn how conditions change over time. A trading agent would use a market environment to practice decisions and learn from the outcomes. The group has described the research program, and comparable public results are sparse.

labs.fit_note: The public site describes research and trading operations at a high level. It provides little detail on a distinct model or training method.

labs.name: Reflection AI
labs.focus: Trained Beam and tested how to make it solve problems with fewer reasoning steps.

innovation.assessment: Reflection trained Beam to reward correct answers and charge a cost for unnecessary reasoning steps. It reports that shorter answers worked better early in training, and that allowing longer reasoning later helped on harder tasks. The lab released the model weights.

labs.name: Reka AI
labs.focus: Builds a family of models that can work with several kinds of input at different sizes.

people.names: Dani Yogatama, Cyprien de Masson d'Autume, Yi Tay, Qi Liu

innovation.example: Reka Core, Flash, and Edge handle four input types
innovation.assessment: Reka trained three model sizes from scratch to handle text, images, video, and audio. Its report compares how the smaller models and the flagship perform on tasks such as answering questions about images and videos.

labs.name: Rhoda AI
labs.focus: Trains robots to act using video and examples of robot movements.

innovation.assessment: Rhoda’s model predicts what the robot should see a short time into the future. A second model translates those frames into movements. The robot repeats the cycle as it moves. Rhoda reports that it learned selected multi-step tasks using about ten hours of robot data.

labs.name: Ricursive Intelligence
labs.focus: Develops AI for chip design and trained its own open-weight language model.

innovation.assessment: Ricursive trained and released Ripple-65B, a language model designed to read long inputs. The public tests compare it with other coding models, which gives researchers an early look at its software skills. Results on chip design remain a separate step.

labs.name: RLWRLD
labs.focus: Trains dexterous robot hands to act using touch and force alongside camera views.

innovation.example: RLDX-1.1 uses touch and force to guide robot hands
innovation.assessment: A camera shows where a cup is. Force readings can tell a robot how the load changes while it pours. RLDX combines these signals with the position of the fingers to choose movements for jobs such as pouring or rotating an object in its hand. The November update keeps the same model design and reports smoother motion and better results on the team’s benchmarks.

labs.name: RODIN
labs.focus: Trained a French-focused language model from scratch and released the weights.
labs.size: Model card reports a single developer.

innovation.assessment: RODIN-1B gives researchers a working model built for French. They can test its French abilities directly or adapt it to their own tasks. The release makes that possible at a small enough size to use as a research starting point.

labs.name: RWKV
labs.focus: Develops language models that keep a running summary of the text they read.
labs.size: Started by Bo Peng. Now a broader project.

innovation.assessment: At each step, RWKV updates a summary of the text it has read. That summary stays the same size as the text gets longer, which helps keep memory use in check. How well the model remembers earlier details depends on the version and the task.

labs.name: Sakana AI
labs.focus: Experiments with a model that uses the timing of its own internal activity to work through a problem.

team.people: David Ha, Ren Ito, Llion Jones
team.background: Ha led Google Brain’s Tokyo research team. Jones co-authored the Transformer paper.

people.names: David Ha, Ren Ito, Llion Jones

innovation.assessment: The Continuous Thought Machine takes several internal steps before it answers. It uses the timing of which artificial neurons activate together to decide what happens in the next step. Sakana demonstrated that approach on mazes.

labs.name: Sapient Intelligence
labs.focus: Tests a reasoning model that works through a problem at two different speeds.

innovation.assessment: HRM alternates between two modules that work at different speeds and repeatedly revises an answer to a grid puzzle. ARC Prize measured 32% on its hidden ARC-AGI-1 set. Its follow-up found that repeated revision explained more of the score than the two-module design alone.

labs.name: Sarvam AI
labs.focus: Released two open models trained for Indian languages and general reasoning.

innovation.assessment: Sarvam trained and released two model sizes and tested them on Indian languages. The release gives researchers openly available models for those languages at that scale.

labs.name: Scaled Cognition
labs.focus: Trains models to handle customer-service tasks that involve using software tools.

innovation.assessment: APT-1 is built for tasks where an agent must make several tool calls and respond to what each tool returns. Scaled Cognition reports higher task completion than the models it compared against on τ-bench and ComplexFuncBench, averaged over ten runs.

labs.name: Sereact
labs.focus: Develops models that let warehouse robots adapt a familiar task from a few video examples.

innovation.assessment: The operator shows the robot a few short videos of the new job. Cortex 2.5 uses those examples as instructions, so the operator can change which item the robot picks from a bin without retraining it. The team tested short variations of tasks the model already knew within the same domain.

labs.name: Sesame
labs.focus: Builds speech models that use earlier turns of a conversation to decide how the next line should sound.

innovation.assessment: Sesame’s CSM uses the conversation so far to shape delivery as well as produce speech. That gives it context for tone and pacing when it speaks the next line. The released model shows how this works in generated audio.

labs.name: Simile
labs.focus: Models how people might respond to surveys and compares the results with real answers.

people.names: Joon Sung Park, Michael Bernstein, Percy Liang, Lainie Yallen

innovation.evidence: Company validation example with observed comparison
innovation.example: Simulated survey answers tested against observed behavior
innovation.assessment: Simile uses AI agents to estimate how groups of people would answer a question. In one test it reports, the model estimated that 93% of a Florida food-delivery cohort would tip. Actual transaction data put it at about 87%.

labs.name: Skild AI
labs.focus: Trains robot models to learn new tasks from examples and work across different hardware.

innovation.example: S1 learns a manipulation task in context from one video
innovation.assessment: Skild’s S1 uses a video of a task as an instruction for the robot. The lab compares this with describing the task in words and reports that demonstrations helped on unfamiliar tasks. This matters for movements that are easier to show than to explain.

labs.name: Sooth Labs
labs.focus: Researches models that predict the odds of real-world events.

people.names: Chuck Hoover, Yaser Sheikh, Ruslan Salakhutdinov, David LaRose, Shih-En Wei

innovation.assessment: Sooth wants a model to answer questions about what may happen next with probabilities. A useful test would ask whether events it calls 70% likely occur about 70% of the time. Its public material describes that aim.

labs.name: SpAItial
labs.focus: Builds models that generate a 3D scene you can explore from different angles.

people.names: Matthias Niessner, Luke Rogers, Ricardo Martin-Brualla, David Novotny

innovation.example: Echo-2 creates 3D scenes that can be revisited
innovation.assessment: Echo-2 takes a prompt or image and generates a 3D scene. In the public demo, a character moves through it and the layout stays in place as the camera turns or returns to an area.

labs.name: Standard Intelligence
labs.focus: Trains computer-use models to learn actions from video of software in use.

team.background: The lab builds models for computer use from video, and publishes work on conversational speech.

innovation.evidence: Lab research release and CAD demonstrations
innovation.assessment: FDM-1 learns computer actions from screen recordings. A separate model estimates clicks and keystrokes by watching what changes on screen, giving FDM-1 actions to learn from. The public demos show continuous mouse control through basic CAD steps.

labs.name: StentorLabs
labs.focus: Documents what a solo developer can train with free computing resources.
labs.size: Project writeup identifies a solo developer.

team.background: Pretrained and studied Portimbria using free compute.

innovation.assessment: Portimbria is a public record of training a small model with free compute. The creator shows how they changed the model size and how much text it could read at once. That makes the project a concrete reference for other developers working under similar constraints.

labs.name: stmonty (lePokeRed)
labs.focus: Trained a small world model to recreate game dynamics from gameplay.

team.background: Individual publisher.

innovation.example: Small world model trained on Pokémon Red gameplay
innovation.assessment: The developer trained a small model to reproduce what happens on screen in Pokémon Red. Other researchers can inspect the experiment. Its results cover that one game.

labs.name: Subquadratic
labs.focus: Develops models that can work with long documents while doing fewer calculations.

people.names: Justin Dangel, Alexander Whedon, Ashley Miyasaki

innovation.assessment: SubQ 1.1 Small sends its attention to selected parts of a long input, reducing how much the model has to compare. The technical report shows it can still find a fact hidden in the input. Reasoning across information scattered through a long document is a different challenge.

labs.name: Talkie
labs.focus: Trained a 13B language model on pre-1931 text to study knowledge and generalization.

team.people: Nick Levine, David Duvenaud, Alec Radford
team.background: The three researchers published the Talkie 13B historical language model.

people.names: Nick Levine, David Duvenaud, Alec Radford

innovation.assessment: Talkie 13B was trained on text published before 1931. In the release, the authors test how surprising later news events are to the model. The cutoff gives researchers a way to study what a model trained on one era can anticipate about the next.

labs.name: theyur (Dhamma Parrot)
labs.focus: Trained a tiny GPT-style model to see what it would learn from a collection of meditation texts.
labs.size: Model card describes a personal project.

innovation.assessment: Derevianko trained a 5.6-million-parameter model from scratch using 51 documents about Vipassana meditation. The model card reports how often it repeated itself and how closely its output matched passages in the training texts.

labs.name: Thinking Machines Lab
labs.focus: Builds reasoning models and tools that let researchers train and test their own model updates.

team.background: Team members have worked on ChatGPT, Character.AI, PyTorch, OpenAI Gym, and Segment Anything.

people.names: Mira Murati, John Schulman, Soumith Chintala

innovation.assessment: In the release demo, an Inkling-based agent used Tinker to train a model, load the updated weights, and test its output on a writing task. The example shows the training and testing loop the agent ran.

labs.name: Tilde Research
labs.focus: Tests changes to attention and training to see how much models learn at a given size and compute budget.

team.background: The lab works on mechanistic interpretability, model architectures, and pretraining.

innovation.example: Parallax changes how attention combines past tokens
innovation.assessment: Parallax replaces the usual weighted average in attention with a learned local linear estimate. The authors report lower prediction error than softmax attention in their 0.6B and 1.7B training runs, including comparisons at similar model size and compute.

labs.name: TypeSafe AI
labs.focus: Trains Jev to make decisions in a format that software can use directly.

people.names: Diogo Moitinho de Almeida, Erik Gafni, Sasha Sheng

innovation.assessment: An application tells Jev what choices are allowed, and Jev returns a decision with an estimate of confidence. A program can use that result to choose its next step. TypeSafe designed the model around that narrow job and demonstrated it in an agent that plays Doom.

labs.name: Tzafon
labs.focus: Trains Northstar to operate software by interpreting what is on the screen.

mentions.title: Tzafon nomination
mentions.author: jessicapeltz
mentions.note: A reply naming the computer-use model lab. The original chart had a higher valuation threshold.

innovation.example: Northstar CUA Fast completes desktop tasks
innovation.assessment: Northstar CUA Fast uses screenshots to choose actions in desktop apps. Tzafon reports 53.1% success on the first attempt across 369 OSWorld tasks. It published the four-billion-parameter model’s weights.

labs.name: Unconventional AI
labs.focus: Tests whether physical circuits could do some of the calculations an AI model needs.

people.names: Naveen Rao, MeeLan Lee, Michael Carbin, Sara Achour

innovation.example: Un-0 image generation with coupled oscillators
innovation.assessment: Un-0 generates images using a simulation of interacting oscillators. That gives the team a way to test a model designed around how physical circuits behave. Running it on real hardware would show whether the approach changes the time and energy needed to generate an image.

labs.name: VeroLM
labs.focus: Trains tiny language models from scratch that read text one byte at a time.

innovation.assessment: Most language models split text into chunks before reading it. VeroLM starts with the raw bytes that make up the text. Its small released model gives researchers a way to test whether that choice helps compared with chunking text at the same model size.

labs.name: WAR Enterprise
labs.focus: Trained a Portuguese-first small language model from scratch.
labs.size: Release post describes an independent developer.

team.background: Release post describes an independent developer.

innovation.assessment: WAR Enterprise released a 200M model trained primarily on Portuguese. The weights let readers test how it responds in Portuguese. The model card leaves the effect of the Portuguese-heavy training data unmeasured.

labs.name: Warp Sciences
labs.focus: Builds automated chemistry research infrastructure.

innovation.assessment: Warp describes a lab that automates chemistry experiments. Public material explains the lab setup. It has yet to show what a specific model contributes.

labs.name: Wayve
labs.focus: Trains models that generate interactive driving scenes to test how a vehicle’s AI responds.

innovation.assessment: GAIA-4 generates driving scenes that change in response to the driving model’s actions. This lets Wayve test what happens after the model makes a decision in simulation. The report leaves open how simulator scores translate to performance on the road.

labs.name: World Labs
labs.focus: Trains spatial world models that generate navigable 3D scenes.

team.people: Fei-Fei Li, Justin Johnson, Ben Mildenhall, Christoph Lassner
team.background: The founding team works across computer vision, graphics, and generative AI.

people.names: Fei-Fei Li, Justin Johnson, Ben Mildenhall, Christoph Lassner

innovation.assessment: Given images or video, Atlas estimates depth and generates new views while keeping the scene consistent as the camera moves. The lab shows how it exports 3D scenes and simulates cameras moving through real spaces.
innovation.note: Marble, released in November 2025, generates explorable 3D scenes. Atlas builds on the same type of 3D representation and also reconstructs scenes from video.

labs.name: X Square Robot
labs.focus: Trains general-purpose robot models and tests which physical tasks they learn before task-specific tuning.

people.names: Qian Wang, Hao Wang, Qian Yang, Hao Pang

innovation.example: Wall-OSS-0.5 tests pretrained skills on real robots
innovation.assessment: The team ran its broadly pretrained model on a 17-task physical test suite before giving it extra training for those tasks. The team reports that it completed several jobs, including one involving a flexible object held out from training. The experiment helps separate what the robot learned during broad training from what it picked up during task-specific practice.

labs.name: Xaira Therapeutics
labs.focus: Combines machine learning and experimental science for drug discovery.

people.names: Marc Tessier-Lavigne, David Baker, Arvind Rajpal, Vikram Bajaj, others

innovation.assessment: Xaira describes using AI and experiments to find potential new drugs. The public overview lays out its research program. Whether a candidate works in patients depends on the results of clinical studies.

labs.name: Zyphra
labs.focus: Builds models that carry a compact record of earlier inputs and use attention where it helps.

people.names: Krithik Puthalath, Danny Martinelli, Tomás Figliolia, Beren Millidge

innovation.example: Zamba2-VL applies a hybrid model design to images
innovation.assessment: Zamba2-VL carries a compact record of earlier inputs and uses attention in selected layers. Zyphra reports a faster first response than comparable Transformer models in its tests. It also found that adding more document and text-in-image examples helped close a recognition gap.
